title: Rooms with a record over SQLite's size limit can't load into Durable Object storage
reason: Reports a large individual JSON record exceeding Cloudflare Durable Object SQLite's string/blob limit during migration from R2. This differs from an oversized total room, and no comments were available.

varveAssessment.assessment: Cloudflare Durable Object SQLite storage is not used by Varve's local document persistence.

title: OG thumbnail renders for shared files time out repeatedly
reason: Reports thousands of production Browser Rendering timeouts over months; the only comment says the issue remained the largest sync-worker incident with hundreds of repeated failures per day. This is a recurring service-availability problem rather than a single transient report.

varveAssessment.assessment: Varve does not run the upstream hosted thumbnail queue or Cloudflare Browser Rendering service.

title: tldraw.com fails to load on browsers without Object.hasOwn
reason: The issue identifies unguarded module-load `Object.hasOwn` calls that blank the app on pre-Chrome 93/Safari 15.4/Firefox 92 browsers. The reply says the issue continued to affect users; no polyfill/fallback resolution is recorded.

varveAssessment.assessment: Varve's supported browser floor and module-load use of `Object.hasOwn` were not audited; applicability remains uncertain until compared against its compatibility policy.

title: Zero IndexedDB-missing errors surface as unhandled rejections
reason: Reports uncaught rejection when Zero's IndexedDB cache disappears at runtime after browser eviction, site-data clearing, or another tab/profile cleanup. No comments were available.

varveAssessment.assessment: The cache belongs to the upstream Zero sync client. Varve's own offline persistence remains a separate durability surface and needs its own inspection.

title: tldraw UI renders in serif font when the host page sets no font family
reason: Reports SDK UI inheriting the browser's default serif font on a plain host page. The reply questions whether this is a real integration problem and values the visible contrast in a from-scratch demo, so the default sans-serif outcome is not accepted as an obvious fix.

varveAssessment.assessment: Varve owns its own UI theme/font tokens and is not embedded as a tldraw SDK; no local font-family defect is established.

title: Deep review of @tldraw/state for bugs and performance improvements
reason: The issue rolls up state bugs (stale computed values, re-entrant/zero-dependency effects, nested rollback, async rollback, computed inheritance/first-derive errors, epoch diffs) plus an allocation optimization and docs. The reply confirms the split fixes merged. Several semantic questions were explicitly left unchanged; they are not included as solved defects.

varveAssessment.assessment: These behaviors belong to upstream @tldraw/state. Varve has distinct history and state systems; compare the specific semantic risks against local transactions/reactive providers before transferring fixes.

title: Deep review of sync and local persistence for correctness bugs
reason: Rolls up fixes for reconnect/socket races, version compatibility, wire chunking, transaction rollback, room/storage behavior, and local IndexedDB persistence. It includes an especially relevant local-persistence PR (#10102) for lost final edits and cross-tab edits during load; the split PRs require recursive evidence review before any Varve conclusion.

varveAssessment.assessment: Most listed work depends on upstream sync/server infrastructure. PR #10102 concerns client-side persistence durability and is queued for direct comparison with Varve's save/close/recovery lifecycle before disposition.

title: Simplify pass across packages, dotcom, and templates
reason: Tracks broad behavior-preserving cleanup split across editor, SDK, dotcom, state, commenting, Mermaid, and templates. The issue body marks some child PRs open and others merged/closed at C1; this is not evidence of functional defects or a license to mechanically refactor Varve code.

varveAssessment.assessment: This is an upstream repository cleanup inventory, not a finding that Varve's modules need the same refactors.

title: Deep review of the select tool and default tool states for bugs
reason: The rollup covers crop sessions, pointer cancellation, locked/rotated shapes, deleted shapes during gestures, clone cancellation, resize/handles and tool transitions. Its sole comment says every split PR merged or closed, with #10071 only a rebase note. This is a large source of concrete regression scenarios, but upstream implementation details and tests require per-PR review before Varve transfer.

varveAssessment.assessment: The user-visible failure modes are relevant to Varve's canvas interaction surface, but each must be compared with its existing pointer/crop/transform invariant and real-interaction coverage rather than imported mechanically.

title: Deep review of the default shape utils and shape tools for bugs
reason: Rolls up fixes across text, tool state, arrows, freehand, lines, geometry, images/video, frames, embeds, and bookmarks, with cases including rotated/scaled parents, degenerate geometry, stale caches, and cancellation. Each child PR is a distinct evidence node; no aggregate conclusion substitutes for reviewing the relevant fixes/tests.

varveAssessment.assessment: Highly relevant regression-scenario source for Varve's draw, arrow, frame, crop, text and media workflows. Individual linked PRs and their tests need review to identify truly shared failure modes and local validation gaps.
